articles.title: Quick Heal Flags the Four Diwali Shopping Scams Most Likely to Reach Your Phone
articles.excerpt: Lookalike stores, fake support numbers, OTP-hunting 'delivery executives' and QR-code refunds are this season's traps — plus the checks that stop each one.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora shoppers sending gifts and money to India this Diwali face the same UPI and lookalike-store traps — the PIN rule applies across borders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Reach stores through bookmarks or official apps
steps.detail: Never shop through links in WhatsApp, SMS or social-media ads — type the address yourself and read the URL for swapped or added letters.

steps.step: Never share an OTP or scan a refund QR code
steps.detail: A UPI PIN only authorises money leaving your account; receiving a refund never requires it. Delivery staff never need your OTP to confirm an address.

steps.step: Check the recipient name and amount before approving any UPI payment
steps.detail: Scammers rename accounts to look like brands. Verify before you approve, and enable payment limits to cap exposure.

steps.step: Turn on multi-factor authentication and unique passwords
steps.detail: Use different passwords for shopping, email and banking, keep apps and browsers updated, and watch transaction alerts for unauthorised activity.

steps.step: If money is gone, report immediately
steps.detail: In India, call the national cybercrime helpline 1930 and file a report at cybercrime.gov.in, then contact your bank to block the card or flag the transaction.

articles.title: How to Make Marble Clay Diyas for Diwali, Step by Step
articles.excerpt: White clay, bright colours rolled to a marbled 1/4 inch, a pinched tip, 45 minutes in the oven and gold rims — a Diwali craft children can actually do.
articles.image_caption: A clay diya, the traditional oil lamp decorated and lit for Diwali (file photo)
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families can make marble diyas this weekend with standard US craft-store clay and tea lights, a day ahead of Diwali gatherings.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.detail: Line a baking tray with parchment paper; roll white clay out as the base layer with a rolling pin.
Place cubes of coloured clay on the white, roll together and work by hand to a 1/4-inch thickness; stacking colours before rolling changes the swirl.
Cut a round with a cookie cutter or small bowl, shape it into a small bowl, and pinch one tip to a point.
Bake on the tray in a preheated oven at 265 degrees F for 45 minutes.
Cool to room temperature, paint the rims gold, and let the paint dry.
Set a tea light in each finished diya instead of oil and a wick for a mess-free lamp.
